transcript.text: My Dyson V10 Absolute (SV12) won't run at all now. On the battery display there's a red light flashing when I press the trigger, then nothing. It was charging overnight. Do I need a new battery or is the whole thing dead?

A flashing red light when pressing the trigger usually means the battery protection has cut in because the voltage is too low, or the battery itself has failed. It doesn't necessarily mean the whole machine is dead, but we need to check if it's actually taking a charge. Please tell me: when you plug the V10 into the wall charger, does any light come on (on the charger brick or at the connection point), and what colour is it?
Yes, the charger light is on (I tried the hallway socket too, same thing). Blue lights come on on the battery display while it's charging, but sometimes it then shows the flashing red as well.

The flashing red light usually means the battery protection circuit has cut in because the voltage is too low to start the motor, even if the lights show some charge. Since the blue lights come on while charging but it still won't run, we need to see if the battery is actually accepting a full charge or if it's failing under load. Please tell me: when you leave it on the charger, do the blue lights stay solid for a while and then go off (indicating a full charge), or does it flash red again as soon as you take it off the charger?

I'm not sure about the solid-then-off bit, I haven't watched it that closely. When I take it off the charger and press the trigger it's just the flashing red again, no blue. For what it's worth, the battery isn't swollen, hot or smelly.

The flashing red light means the battery protection has cut in because the voltage is too low to start the motor. This usually happens when a battery is deeply discharged or failing under load, but we need to rule out a charger issue first.

Ok. How do I rule out the charger? I've already tried a different socket and the charger light comes on, and I charged it for 3.5 hours plugged straight into the battery rather than the dock, same result.

To rule out the charger, the most reliable method is to test with a known-good battery. If you borrow another V10 battery and it starts up normally on your machine, your original battery has failed (likely due to deep discharge damage) and needs replacing. If it still flashes red and won't run on the second battery, then the issue is likely your charger or the charging contacts on the vacuum body itself.

I don't have a spare V10 battery to swap in and nobody I know has one. Is there any other way to tell whether it's the battery or the machine? I'd rather not take anything apart until I've spoken to Dyson about cost.

Since you cannot borrow a spare battery and the charger is confirmed working (the light comes on), we are left with two possibilities: the battery has degraded to the point where it can no longer hold enough voltage to start the motor, or there is an internal fault in the vacuum's charging circuit. Given that it flashes red immediately upon trying to run despite being charged for 3.5 hours, a failed battery is the most probable cause. I recommend contacting Dyson support directly. They can often diagnose this remotely or arrange a repair/replacement. If the vacuum is out of warranty, they will be able to give you an exact cost for a new battery versus a full unit replacement, which helps you decide whether it's worth repairing.
